source_refs.note: Exercise 3.5, Question 6 (i)-(iii): substitution and an odd integrand; book p. 102. Key on p. 300 under 'Exercise 3.2'.

blocks.prompt: 6 (i) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{0}^{4} x\sqrt{4 - x}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan \(x\) aur \(\sqrt{4 - x}\) ka product hai; root ki wajah se seedha formula nahi lagta.
Diya kya hai? \(x\sqrt{4 - x}\) aur limits \(0\) se \(4\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Rule kaunsa? \(t = 4 - x\) rakhenge. Is se root \(\sqrt{t}\) ban jata hai aur \(x = 4 - t\), yani sab kuch \(t\) ki powers mein aa jata hai.
Plan: substitution, limits badalna, power rule.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{0}^{4} x\sqrt{4 - x}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: definite integral mein substitution \(t = 4 - x\) (asal mein yeh Property IV jaisa hi kaam hai). Root ke andar wali cheez ko naya variable bana dena aise sawalon ka aam tareeqa hai.

Substitution aur nayi limits
\[t = 4 - x,\quad x = 4 - t,\quad dx = -dt\]
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow t = 4,\quad x = 4 \Rightarrow t = 0\]
\[\int_{4}^{0} (4 - t)\sqrt{t}\,(-dt)\]
\[= \int_{0}^{4} (4t^{1/2} - t^{3/2})\,dt\]
Kyun: \(dx = -dt\) wala minus limits ko seedha karne mein istemal hua (Property II: limits ulto to sign ulto). Phir \((4 - t)t^{1/2} = 4t^{1/2} - t^{3/2}\) multiply kiya.
Dhyan dein: limits bhi badalni hain; \(x = 0\) par \(t = 4\) hai, \(t = 0\) nahi.

Integrate karein
\[= \left[\dfrac{8}{3}t^{3/2} - \dfrac{2}{5}t^{5/2}\right]_{0}^{4}\]
Kyun: \(\int t^{1/2}dt = \frac{t^{3/2}}{3/2} = \frac{2}{3}t^{3/2}\) (aur 4 se multiply to \(\frac{8}{3}\)), aur \(\int t^{3/2}dt = \frac{2}{5}t^{5/2}\). Fraction power se divide karna yani us ka ulta multiply karna.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{128}{15} \approx 8.53\]
Kyun: integrand dono kinaron par 0 hai aur \(x = \frac{8}{3}\) par sab se bara (taqreeban 3.08). Is liye area \(4 \times 3.08 \approx 12.3\) se kam aur 0 se kaafi zyada hona chahiye; 8.53 munasib hai. Answer key mein bhi \(\frac{128}{15}\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 6 (ii) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{0}^{1} \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1 - x}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan neeche \(\sqrt{1 - x}\) hai. \(x = 1\) ke qareeb integrand bohat bara ho jata hai, lekin area phir bhi mehdood (finite) aata hai.
Diya kya hai? \(\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1 - x}}\) aur limits \(0\) se \(1\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Rule kaunsa? \(t = 1 - x\) rakhenge; phir \(x^2 = (1 - t)^2\) aur neeche \(\sqrt{t}\). Expand kar ke har term ko \(t^{1/2}\) se divide karenge to sirf powers bachengi.
Plan: substitution, expand, divide, power rule.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{0}^{1} \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1 - x}}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: substitution \(t = 1 - x\), \((1 - t)^2\) ka expansion, har term ko \(t^{1/2}\) se divide, phir power rule.

Substitution aur nayi limits
\[t = 1 - x,\quad x = 1 - t,\quad dx = -dt\]
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow t = 1,\quad x = 1 \Rightarrow t = 0\]
\[\int_{1}^{0} \dfrac{(1 - t)^2}{\sqrt{t}}(-dt) = \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{(1 - t)^2}{\sqrt{t}}\,dt\]
Kyun: \(dx = -dt\) ka minus limits ko seedha karne mein kharch hua. Ab neeche sirf \(\sqrt{t}\) hai, jo aasaan hai.

Expand aur divide karein
\[\dfrac{1 - 2t + t^2}{t^{1/2}} = t^{-1/2} - 2t^{1/2} + t^{3/2}\]
Kyun: \((1 - t)^2 = 1 - 2t + t^2\). Har term ko \(t^{1/2}\) se divide karne ka matlab hai power mein se \(\frac{1}{2}\) ghatana: \(t^0 \to t^{-1/2}\), \(t^1 \to t^{1/2}\), \(t^2 \to t^{3/2}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}} = t^{-1/2}\) hai, negative power; yeh sign ghalat na ho.

Integrate karein
\[\left[2t^{1/2} - \dfrac{4}{3}t^{3/2} + \dfrac{2}{5}t^{5/2}\right]_{0}^{1}\]
\[= 2 - \dfrac{4}{3} + \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{30 - 20 + 6}{15} = \dfrac{16}{15}\]
Kyun: power rule: \(\int t^{-1/2}dt = 2t^{1/2}\), \(\int 2t^{1/2}dt = \frac{4}{3}t^{3/2}\), \(\int t^{3/2}dt = \frac{2}{5}t^{5/2}\). \(t = 0\) par sab zero. Ghaur karein: \(t^{-1/2}\) bara hota hai lekin us ka antiderivative \(2t^{1/2}\) mehdood rehta hai, isi liye area finite hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(2t^{1/2} - \dfrac{4}{3}t^{3/2} + \dfrac{2}{5}t^{5/2}\right)\]
\[= t^{-1/2} - 2t^{1/2} + t^{3/2} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: antiderivative ka derivative wapas integrand deta hai, to integration sahi hai. Answer key mein bhi \(\frac{16}{15}\) hai.

blocks.explanation:
Interval \([-1, 1]\) zero ke ird gird barabar (symmetric) hai. Aise interval par sab se pehle dekhte hain ke integrand even hai ya odd.
Diya kya hai? \(\frac{e^x - 1}{e^x + 1}\) aur limits \(-1\) se \(1\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Rule kaunsa? Property V: agar function odd ho, yani \(f(-x) = -f(x)\), to symmetric interval par integral seedha 0 hai, koi antiderivative nahi chahiye.
Plan: \(f(-x)\) nikalna, \(e^x\) se multiply kar ke simplify, phir Property V.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{e^x - 1}{e^x + 1}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: Property V: \(f(-x) = -f(x)\) ho to \(\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 0\). Symmetric limits dekhte hi yeh test karna aadat bana lein.

\(f(-x)\) nikalein
\[f(-x) = \dfrac{e^{-x} - 1}{e^{-x} + 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 - e^{x}}{1 + e^{x}}\]
Kyun: \(x\) ki jagah \(-x\) rakha, phir upar neeche \(e^{x}\) se multiply kiya taa ke negative power khatam ho: \(e^{-x} \cdot e^{x} = e^0 = 1\).

\(f(x)\) se muqabla karein
\[\dfrac{1 - e^{x}}{1 + e^{x}} = -\dfrac{e^{x} - 1}{e^{x} + 1} = -f(x)\]
Kyun: \(1 - e^x = -(e^x - 1)\); upar se minus bahar nikala. Is liye \(f\) odd function hai.
Dhyan dein: odd/even ka faisla \(f(-x)\) ko poori tarah simplify kar ke hi karein; adhoori shakal dekh kar andaza na lagayein.

Property V lagayein
\[\int_{-1}^{1} \dfrac{e^x - 1}{e^x + 1}\,dx = 0\]
Kyun: odd function ka graph origin ke ird gird ulta hota hai: ek taraf jitna area axis ke upar, doosri taraf utna hi neeche. Dono cancel ho jate hain.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{e^x - 1}{e^x + 1} = \tanh\dfrac{x}{2}\]
Kyun: upar neeche \(e^{x/2}\) se divide karein to \(\frac{e^{x/2} - e^{-x/2}}{e^{x/2} + e^{-x/2}}\) banta hai, jo \(\tanh\frac{x}{2}\) hai, ek jaana pehchana odd function. Answer key mein bhi 0 hai.
